- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to align with mean-reversion bias.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true outcome by >5%), model frequently overcorrects; reduce forecast by 2–5% in next period.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often lags; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% in the 3rd–5th period of forecast window.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is volatile (alternating ±0.33) — increase forecast by 1–2% to compensate for uncertainty.
- For 30-day forecasts, mean reversion is strong in 2024 Q4; if forecast > 75, reduce by 2–4% in next 3–5 periods unless sentiment strongly supports.
- If sentiment is 1.00 for 3+ consecutive days, model tends to overfit; cap forecast at 10% above recent 7-day average to avoid overshoot.
